one_liner: internal dashboard based on our excel files with financials

actors.name: Owner
actors.description: Business owner who reviews overall financial health and profitability.

actors.name: Bookkeeper
actors.description: Maintains the underlying figures, uploads and reconciles the Excel files.

actors.name: Manager
actors.description: Department or project lead who checks budgets versus actuals for their area.

actors.name: Accountant
actors.description: External advisor who reviews numbers at month- and year-end.

nouns.name: Monthly Summary
nouns.description: A roll-up of income, expenses and profit for a given month.

nouns.name: Revenue Line
nouns.description: A single source of income within a period.

nouns.name: Expense Line
nouns.description: A single cost item within a period.

nouns.name: Cost Category
nouns.description: A grouping label used to classify expenses and revenue.

nouns.name: Budget
nouns.description: A planned amount for a category or department over a period.

nouns.name: Cash Balance
nouns.description: Money on hand across accounts at a point in time.

nouns.name: Excel Upload
nouns.description: A source spreadsheet imported to refresh the dashboard.
nouns.example: financials_march2024.xlsx uploaded by Bookkeeper on Apr 2

nouns.name: Department
nouns.description: A part of the business that revenue and costs are attributed to.

nouns.name: KPI
nouns.description: A tracked headline figure shown on the dashboard.

actions.example: Bookkeeper matches account balance to bank statement
Corrects rent vendor name to Regus
Owner checks gross margin against target
Manager checks Marketing planned vs actual
Accountant exports Q1 summary for filing
Owner sets Q2 marketing budget to $18,000

rules.text: Only the Owner and Accountant may view whole-company profit and cash balances; Managers see only their own department.
rules.example: Sales manager cannot open payroll totals

rules.text: A month cannot show a Monthly Summary until its Excel Upload for that period has been imported.
rules.example: March summary hidden until financials_march2024.xlsx is uploaded

rules.text: Total income minus total expenses must equal the net profit shown for every month.
Every Revenue Line and Expense Line must belong to exactly one Cost Category.
rules.example: An uncategorized $500 charge is flagged before summary is final

rules.text: Only the Bookkeeper may upload or edit source figures; Owner and Manager view only.
rules.example: Owner cannot change an expense amount directly

rules.text: Uploading a new file for a period replaces that period's figures rather than adding to them.
rules.example: Re-uploading March overwrites, not duplicates, March lines

rules.text: All amounts are held in one currency (USD) across the dashboard.
rules.example: A EUR invoice must be converted before entry

rules.text: The dashboard reflects internal figures only and is never shared outside the company.
(integrity) Every change to figures — uploads, edits, reconciliations, categorizations — must be recorded in an unalterable log showing who changed what and when, retained for the accounting year.
(integrity) A Revenue Line or Expense Line cannot be saved without its required fields (amount, category, and period/date) completed.
(state) Each Excel Upload's imported figures are versioned so a prior period's numbers can be restored if a re-upload is wrong.
(integrity) Every Budget must reference a valid Cost Category or Department, and every Department's figures must trace to existing Revenue and Expense Lines — no orphaned links.
(integrity) Duplicate Revenue or Expense Lines (same source/vendor, amount, and period) are flagged or rejected to prevent double-counting.
(scope) Users interact with financials only through the dashboard; no one accesses or edits the underlying Excel files or database directly.

non_goals.text: Does not send or generate invoices to customers.
Does not connect directly to bank accounts to pull live transactions.
Does not file taxes or produce official accounting statements.
Does not let external clients log in or view any figures.
Does not process payments or payroll.

decisions.question: Who needs an account to use the app?

options.label: Nobody logs in — one person uses it on their own device
Exactly one person logs in (the owner)
Several people log in, possibly with different powers

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: Owner, Bookkeeper, Manager and Accountant all use it with different powers.

decisions.question: Do different people have different powers?

options.label: Everyone who logs in can do everything
An owner/admin plus staff with fewer powers
Admins define their own roles and permissions

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: r1/r5 define an owner/admin plus staff (bookkeeper edits, others view) with differing powers.

decisions.question: Is this for one business, or will many separate businesses use it with their data kept apart?

options.label: One business (ours)
Many separate businesses, each seeing only its own data

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: r8: reflects one business's internal figures only.

decisions.question: How do additional people get access?

options.label: No additional people
An admin invites them
Anyone can sign up themselves

decisions.question: How do people sign in?

options.label: No sign-in
Email + password
Email link, no password
Google/Microsoft sign-in
Company single sign-on (SAML/OIDC)

decisions.question: What happens when two people edit the same thing at once?

options.label: Rare; the last save wins
Common; the app must prevent or merge conflicting edits

decisions.question: Do you need a record of who changed what and when?

options.label: No
Just created/updated by whom and when
A full, viewable history of every change

decisions.question: How does the app reach people when something happens?

options.label: It doesn't — people check the app
Email
Email and SMS
Only inside the app (bell/inbox)

decisions.question: Must it work without internet?

options.label: Online only
Keeps working offline and syncs later

decisions.question: Where is it used?

options.label: In a browser, on desktop and phone
In a browser, mostly on phones
As an installed phone app
As an installed desktop app

decisions.question: Do you start with existing data?

options.label: Start empty
Import from a spreadsheet/CSV once
Migrate from another tool

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: a1/n7/r6: figures come from imported Excel files.

decisions.question: Do people need to get their data out?

options.label: No
Download lists as CSV/Excel
Full export and/or an API

decisions.question: When something is deleted, what really happens?

options.label: It's gone
It's archived and can be restored
Records are never deleted, only voided/cancelled

decisions.question: How much data will there be?

options.label: Hundreds of records
Tens of thousands
Millions

decisions.question: Does it need to connect to other tools?

options.label: No
A few key ones (e.g., accounting, payments, calendar)
Many — it needs a public API / webhooks

decisions.question: Does money move through the app?

options.label: No payments involved
It records payments that happen elsewhere
It collects card/bank payments via a provider
It collects payments and pays out to others (marketplace-style)

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: g5: no payments or payroll processed.

decisions.question: Languages and regions?

options.label: One language, one country
Several languages
Several countries (taxes, formats, currencies)

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: r7: all amounts in one currency (USD).

decisions.question: Can files/photos be attached to things?

options.label: No
Yes — upload and download
Yes — with previews, versions, and sharing

decisions.question: Do some actions need someone else's approval first?

options.label: No
One approver
Multi-step approval chains

decisions.question: Must anything happen automatically on a schedule?

options.label: No
Only reminders/notifications
Records get created automatically (recurring invoices, appointments, reports)

decisions.question: Does it hold data with special legal handling (health, payment cards, minors)?

options.label: Ordinary business data
Personal data needing consent/retention care (GDPR-like)
Regulated data (health, cards, finance)

decisions.question: How long is data kept?

options.label: Until someone deletes it
Auto-removed after a set period
Each business sets its own policy

decisions.question: Can each business customize the app?

options.label: No — everyone gets the same thing
Branding and templates (logo, colors, wording)
Custom fields and workflows

decisions.question: What do people need to see across many records?

options.label: Sortable, filterable lists
A dashboard with totals and counts
Custom reports people build themselves

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: One-liner and archetype: an internal dashboard of totals, budgets and KPIs.

decisions.question: Are records grouped into separate projects/workspaces, or is it one shared pool?

options.label: One shared pool — everything lives in one place with filters
Separate projects/workspaces, each with its own members

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: One company's data in one place, filtered by department; no separate workspaces.

decisions.question: Who can see a record?

options.label: Everyone in the team sees everything
Records are private to their owner unless shared or assigned
Visible within the owner's team/department; admins see all

decisions.question: Who can change a record?

options.label: Anyone who can see it can edit it
Only its owner/assignee and admins; others just view
Set per record: view / comment / edit

decisions.rationale: stated in the description: r5: only the Bookkeeper edits source figures; Owner/Manager view only.

decisions.question: Are the fields on a record fixed, or can admins add their own?

options.label: Fixed — the same fields for everyone
Admins add custom fields (text, number, date, dropdown) to each record type
Admins define whole new record types with their own fields

decisions.question: Are records linked to each other?

options.label: No — each record stands alone
Yes — records of different types reference each other (contact → company → deal)
Yes — including parent/child trees (projects → tasks → sub-tasks)

decisions.question: Can two records be the same thing (same email, same serial number)?

options.label: Allowed — nothing stops duplicates
The app warns about likely duplicates and offers to merge
A key field must be unique; duplicates are rejected

decisions.question: How do people find a record?

options.label: Filter and sort within each list
One search box across all record types
Search that also looks inside comments and attachments

decisions.question: What happens when a Cost Category that still has Revenue/Expense Lines attached is deleted?

options.label: Block deletion until lines are recategorized
Force reassignment to another category first
Allow delete and flag orphaned lines as uncategorized

decisions.question: What happens if the Bookkeeper is editing a line while a new Excel upload replaces that same period?

options.label: Upload overwrites; manual edits are lost
Lock the period during upload; edits blocked
Warn and require manual reconcile of conflicting edits

decisions.question: How is a re-upload of the same period's file handled (e.g. same file uploaded twice)?

options.label: Silently replace the period each time
Detect same period and require confirm before overwrite
Keep each upload as a version and let user pick active

decisions.question: How are negative amounts, zeros, and rounding handled in totals and KPIs?

options.label: Round to cent; allow negatives (refunds/credits)
Reject negative amounts on import
Round only for display, keep full precision internally

decisions.question: How is the period a line belongs to determined when dates cross month boundaries or timezones?

options.label: Use the period declared on the Excel Upload
Derive from each row's date field
Bookkeeper assigns period per upload

decisions.question: What happens when an Excel upload partially fails (some rows invalid/uncategorized)?

options.label: Reject the whole file until fixed
Import valid rows, flag the rest for review
Stage all rows for review before committing

decisions.question: How is a Manager blocked from whole-company profit/cash while still seeing their department, including delegated access?

options.label: Server-side filter by department; no override
Owner can grant temporary broader view
Show company rows but redact restricted figures

decisions.question: Can a completed Excel upload be undone/reverted to the prior period figures?

options.label: No — only a new upload replaces it
Yes — revert to the previously active version
Full version history with restore of any prior import
